subject: Lighthouse hosted API - capacity & budget recap
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Lighthouse hosted API - capacity & budget recap

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and requested next steps so we can put a concrete pricing sketch on paper: 

High-level ask (from Ellen): run Lighthouse's customer-facing assistant (search + summarization + answers) on Redwood hosted API. Important constraints: low tail latency for interactive queries and predictable cost per month.

What we captured on the call (please confirm):
- Typical monthly token volume: 20M–40M tokens/mo (baseline, currently instrumented)
- Seasonal peak / burst windows: mid-month marketing pushes lead to short bursts ~30–45 min where 99th percentile TPS goes to ~85–120 TPS.
- Steady-state peak TPS (99th): 40–60 TPS during business hours.
- Target budget band: $8k–$18k / month (finance indicated mid-range is more realistic)
- Unit economics ask: rough $/1M token target for internal comparison.

Attachments: you mentioned a short usage export — please attach the CSV if possible (we can align unit pricing to actual token shape). I've attached a blank checklist and our standard SLA draft for reference.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Ellen/Tom: confirm monthly volume range + attach usage export (CSV preferred). If you have sequence-length percentiles that will help kernel selection.
2) Karthik: can you produce a two-tier pricing sketch (1) baseline monthly rate for 20–40M tokens with $/1M buckets and (2) burst window guidance for 99th at ~100 TPS including expected concurrency headroom?
3) Monica/Logan: I will draft the initial commercial note + SOW estimate once we have the CSV.

Thanks — want to get a one-pager back to finance and procurement this week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SLA-draft-v2.pdf (pdf stub), lighthouse-usage-export.csv (requested)

Thanks, Monica — short answers and I'm attaching the usage CSV you requested (lighthouse-usage-export.csv). Couple clarifications: 

- The 20M–40M token range is accurate for production traffic (we're at ~25M today, growing ~20% q/q). The lower end is our conservative commitment; the upper represents expected growth if experiments scale.
- Peak details: recent campaign on May 12th had a 32-minute window where 99th TPS peaked at 112 TPS. That campaign included longer context reads (~1.2k tokens avg per session) which pushed tokens-per-query higher.
- For finance, our goal is to land somewhere < $10k/mo but we can stretch to $15k if latency and SLAs are solid.
- Procurement (Tom): we'll need an SOW + clear metric definitions. If you can provide an interim figure for $/1M tokens so we can compare to internal cloud footprint, that would help.

Attaching: lighthouse-usage-export.csv (CSV stub).

—Ellen

Thanks for the CSV, Ellen — that helps. Quick pricing sketch and a couple of clarifying asks so we can model unit economics more precisely.

Pricing sketch (hosted API, non-binding):
- Option A (Commit band): 20–30M tokens/mo 
  - List anchor: $900 / 1M tokens (volume-discount ladder applies at higher bands)
  - Effective monthly cost at 25M: ~$22,500 (note: this is list, we can discount for annual commit)
- Option B (Flex) : pay-as-you-go with burst protection
  - Baseline $1,100 / 1M tokens, included autoscaling for short bursts up to 2x baseline at no extra per-token markup for first 30 minutes per day.
  - For sustained 99th TPS > 80 for >30 min, additional burst premium applies (~+20% tokens during that window).

Observations (from the CSV):
- Your per-session token consumption during campaign windows is higher (mean ~850 tokens/session, 95th ~1.3k). That will increase unit cost when normalized to requests.
- If target budget is <$10k/mo, we would need either a material annual commit discount or to reduce retained context / cache rate. Rough target: to hit $10k at 25M tokens we'd need an effective price of ~$400 / 1M tokens — that implies either a large commit (>12 months) or moving to Dedicated to squeeze infra costs.

Questions to finalize numbers:
1) Can you share percentiles for sequence length (p50/p90/p99) by session? That lets us estimate kernel selection and KV cache hit rate.
2) How many concurrent interactive users at peak (approx) — i.e., how many simultaneous sessions feeding queries into the assistant?
3) Are you open to a hybrid plan: baseline hosted for steady-state and a Dedicated-reserved pool for the marketing campaign windows (we can model a blended unit econ).

I'll prepare two scenarios: a conservative hosted-only price ladder and a blended hosted+dedicated run-rate with estimated committed discount. I can get that back by EOD tomorrow if you can answer the three bullets.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com

1) Sequence length percentiles (session-level): p50 620 tokens, p90 1,050 tokens, p99 1,450 tokens.
2) Concurrent interactive sessions at peak: we observed ~85 simultaneous sessions during the May campaign peak window. That maps to approximately 100–115 TPS given the higher tokens-per-query.
3) We are open to a hybrid approach — procurement is willing to consider a small reserved pool for campaign windows if the blended unit economics are favourable vs pure hosted.

Procurement note (Tom): finance needs an interim $/1M estimate to compare against our internal infra delta. If you can get a conservative hosted-only and a blended hosted+reserved estimate in writing, we can run the numbers this week.
